newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Serfin seen close to breaking even in Q1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Serfin seen close to breaking even in Q1.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Serfin is expected to report a $0.04 per ADR loss in the first quarter, according to the average forecast from a Reuters survey of seven banking analysts.

Some analysts forecast a slight profit, however. The telling factor may be how many reserves against bad loans Serfin created between February 28 -- when it last detailed its asset quality position -- and the end of the quarter.

Whether profit or loss, the result is expected to be a light relief after the stunning $0.76 loss in the previous quarter, and analysts will be watching the report for any sign that Serfin is emerging from a year of gloomy news.
The Q4 loss was largely due to a 2.9 billion peso reserve-building effort prior to the announcement of sale of a 19.9 percent stake to HSBC Holdings PLC 0005.HK for about $300 million in February.

That transaction will not go through until Serfin wraps up a capitalization scheme previously agreed with the government. It also sold a 10.3 billion peso chunk of mortgage loans to the Bank Insurance Fund in February, and the government took a stake roughly equivalent to 17 percent in the bank in exchange.

"They've already created all the provisions they could possibly want," said Carlos Gomez, bank analyst at Paribas, who has the highest forecast of a profit of $0.015 per ADR, or 0.03 pesos per share, a net gain of around 63 million pesos. He said the profit would be Serfin's first in six quarters.

"All the earnings should come from the non-bank subsidiaries, as we expect Banca Serfin just to break even; the bank will probably use its substantial tax credits to balance a negative operating result," Gomez wrote in a report.

Most other analysts expected a loss, except for Merrill Lynch's Rodrigo Quintanilla, who predicted Serfin would continue to create high provisions but thought it would offset the drain with tax credits.

"From an earnings point of view, we think that margins will decline and fee income growth should be subdued. We also anticipate a high level of loan loss provisions that will match continuing charge-offs," said Quintanilla.
"However, it is likely that the bank will derive important tax benefits from these high provisions, and that part of this benefit may materialize in the first quarter.
He expected a slight profit of 0.02 pesos per share, or $0.01 per ADS -- roughly 43 million pesos.
Susana Ornelas, bank analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico City, said she would keep an eye out for possible deposit growth and an improvement in interest margins.
This could represent the first good news at Serfin in more than a year. The bank, Mexico's third largest, has also one of the country's poorest track records.
Other analysts said they expected a slowdown in asset quality deterioration, especially after it offloaded so many problem loans to the government in February.
Up to February 28, it reported that its reserve coverage against past-due loans was around 59.4 percent -- a level that analysts said should remain fairly steady.
